title: Derived Verb Forms — Completing the Set

steps.title: Three more patterns — one hiding, two brand new
body: Form IV was hiding in your vocabulary the whole time, the same way II, III, V, VIII, and X were: أَرَادَ (to want) and أَغْلَقَ (to close) are both Form IV — أَفْعَلَ, أَ prefixed to the root. You've been using أَرَادَ's present tense, أُرِيدُ, since your very first "I would like..." phrase.
Form VI and Form VII needed one genuinely new word each. تَكَاتَبَ (to correspond) is Form VI — تَفَاعَلَ, the reciprocal of Form III — built on ك-ت-ب, the same root as كَتَبَ, كِتَاب, and مَكْتَبَة.

Form VII is the odd one out: اِنْفَتَحَ (it opened) and اِنْغَلَقَ (it closed) never take a person as their subject — a door اِنْفَتَحَ by itself; a person doesn't. That's exactly why they pair so naturally with verbs you already know: فَتَحَ الرَّجُلُ الْبَابَ ("the man opened the door") describes someone doing it; اِنْفَتَحَ الْبَابُ ("the door opened") describes it happening, with no one named as the doer.

steps.title: Three more patterns
steps.intro: Read each sentence, then check which verb form it uses. Tap 🔊 to hear any line.

steps.title: A form you already knew
steps.prompt: أَرَادَ (to want) starts with أَ. Which form is that?
steps.explanation: أَفْعَلَ prefixes أَ to the root — you've said أُرِيدُ (its present tense) many times without naming this pattern until now.

steps.title: No one did it
steps.prompt: اِنْفَتَحَ الْبَابُ فَجْأَةً — who opened the door?

options.label: No one is named — it just happened
The sentence doesn't say, but someone must have

steps.explanation: Form VII (اِنْفَعَلَ) describes something undergoing an action, not someone performing one — that's the whole point of the pattern, not a gap in the sentence.

steps.title: Reciprocal action
steps.prompt: تَكَاتَبَ is Form VI — تَ added to Form III's own pattern. What does Form VI often mean?

options.label: Doing the action to/with each other
Something undergoing an action, with no one performing it
Seeking or considering something to be true

steps.explanation: Form VI's تَ is the reciprocal counterpart of Form III, the same way Form V's تَ is the reflexive counterpart of Form II — تَكَاتَبَ literally means the two sides wrote to each other.

steps.title: b1-u1 is complete
steps.message: Eight of the ten derived forms, all built from a mix of words you already knew and three new ones chosen to fit naturally beside them. Only Form IX — colours and physical defects, a genuinely rare pattern — is still ahead, and it's staying there until much later.
